A missing original Lookup has no new getter-error API; its availability remains false instead of synthesizing nil/error. Missing reference get uses its declared owned sentinel; the original setter still exposes actual NotExistError.

Original CountVarP initializes receiver0 and NoOptDefVal+1, then fixture start is explicitly assigned. Direct opt-in Value.Set exposes original parsed-value mutation even on range error. Reference commits only successful0..2 parses or allowed increment, preserving strconv cause objects. Negative commits explicit values before checking. Option-off -vv still uses original Parse and increments twice. The selected arm64 worker is required for the frozen9223372036854775808 overflow boundary.

Reference uses original ParseAll callbacks and rejects repeated annotated *Flag identity before original Set, so long and shorthand spellings share ownership. Unannotated repeats and separate annotated flags remain independent. Negative compares raw spellings. Its lexical helper also exists in the reference but the exact five vectors fit it; this is not a general parser or prepared unknown-token-report implementation.

Original FlagUsagesWrapped uses DefValue and NoOptDefVal and suppresses hidden flags. Reference renders a shallow Flag copy with redacted display fields while the actual original flag and live Value stay unchanged; it redacts both display defaults and optional value. Negative leaves optional display value exposed. Getter reads the actual parsed flag, preserving PUBLIC_DEFAULT/PUBLIC_OPTION and changed values.

Original FuncP invokes callback through Value.Set during Parse. Reference queues fixed public values through the actual parser and flushes only when parsing succeeded, stopping at first callback failure. Option-off mode remains immediate. Negative flushes from deferred cleanup even on parser failure, while retaining that parse error. Fixed3 queue/trace covers the longest frozen vector; each new row gets fresh state.

Exact TextVar newTextValue copies the complete default struct through reflect, preserving Failure/Typed pointers in the actual receiver. UnmarshalText returns before receiver mutation on the two failure literals and commits public-text on success. Original Set wraps cause with InvalidValueError and exposes original GetFlag/Unwrap. Reference replaces only opt-in invalid-value errors with an owned redacted wrapper preserving actual flag/cause; negative reconstructs a string error and loses those identities. Unknown flag and opt-out paths remain original.

Original OrCompose calls alternatives on the original reflected input3 and stops on nil error, including nil output; on total failure it constructs a concatenated error string and loses original causes. Reference invokes original DecodeHookExec for each fixed typed hook, joins cause objects, accepts nil successful output and returns a declared no-hooks sentinel. Negative continues after nil output. Is/As observations preserve typed hook code7 without uncontrolled generic Error formatting.

Receiver types match the frozen direct, exported squashed, single-remain and ordinary-map schemas and initial states. Original effective discovery keeps the last remain field and later assigns unmatched keys. Reference counts direct and squashed remain tags before Decode and rejects conflicts even on empty data. Negative checks direct fields only. Single-remain and ordinary maps still use original NewDecoder/Decode with declared config values. Captured map values are row-owned and are not reused for later dispatches.

Original getTagValue chooses the first nonempty configured tag. Reference present_first uses reflect.StructTag.Lookup to distinguish empty-present from absent and selects the matching single tag name; a present '-' skips Decode and preserves initial field. Legacy first_nonempty and negative remain original. The reflected one-field receiver is exported/addressable and matches the literal tag/data fixture.
